correctness.rationale: For every positive arm length, a geodesic betweenness obstruction and a three-leaf trace construction prove VC dimension 3. Three independent threshold searches of depth floor(log2(m+1)) provide the all-size online lower bound. The finite class consists exactly of center-containing three-arm prefixes and center-excluding single-arm intervals, giving (m+1)^3+3m(m+1)/2 concepts. Exhaustive graph-growth enumeration independently produces the same concepts. Two independently represented dynamic programs implement the mathematically equivalent complete-tree recurrence, considering all vertices, both labels, and every surviving state, checking all lengths 1..12; 12 has 2431 concepts and depth 9, but depth 10 is excluded. A separately computed root profile covers all 13 first-query types and gives maximum possible root depth 9. Cardinality pruning is a logically necessary condition; there is no sampling, extrapolation, or timeout-based conclusion.

value.rationale: The family of all connected vertex ranges in a three-arm spider is an intrinsic, nonartificial learning concept class. Its fixed VC dimension 3 contrasted with unbounded adaptive dimension is structural, and the exact first two-bit loss against the cardinality bound at twelve arm edges is a motivated finite threshold measuring geometric query imbalance, not an arbitrary sliced statistic. Its exact value and threshold are not supplied by known subtree counts or static VC bounds. The claim explicitly does not extrapolate an all-size online formula.
